Our ability to profitably grow depends on disciplined underwriting and pricing in homeowners and flood, including our ability to appropriately select risks, forecast claims frequency and severity, and respond rapidly to emerging trends.
We believe our “land and expand” strategy, including tailored underwriting, pricing, and product design by geography, will continue to be an important driver of growth.

However, expansion into new states and products (including private flood) presents execution risk, including the risk of mispricing local perils, unexpected regulatory or market constraints, slower-than-expected agency activation, and higher-than-expected losses, which could adversely affect our growth and profitability.
If we obtain additional capital by issuing equity, the interests of our existing shareholders will be diluted.

At each annual renewal, we consider several factors that influence any changes to our reinsurance purchases, including any plans to change the underlying insurance coverage we offer, updated loss activity, the level of our capital and surplus, change in our risk appetite and the cost of availability of reinsurance treaties.
We have a financial strength rating of “A, Exceptional” (Outlook Stable) from Demotech.

The “A, Exceptional” (Outlook Stable) rating obtained by OIG is consistent with our business plan and allows us to actively pursue relationships with the agents and brokers identified in our marketing plan.
Our wholly owned subsidiary, OIC has a financial strength rating of BBB+ (Outlook Stable) from Kroll Bond Rating Agency, LLC (“KBRA”).

Excluding reserves for losses and LAE (for which the timing of payment is not fixed and cannot be determined on an individual or aggregate basis), we expect approximately $12.9 million of these obligations to be due within the next 12 months (primarily scheduled debt principal, interest, and operating lease payments) and approximately $81.4 million to be due thereafter.
Amounts disclosed are gross of anticipated reinsurance recoveries; reinsurance does not discharge our obligations to policyholders, and reinsurance recoverables are reported separately as assets.
We evaluate whether an allowance for expected credit losses is required on reinsurance recoverables.
